registry.title: Proposed Sparq verifiable-credential query method registry

limitations: Native RDF integration from PRs 6504 and 6577 is not in this snapshot and is not described.
sparq-zk import entries are summarized from skills/zk-query-proofs/SKILL.md, not re-read from source.
No build, test or proof was executed to produce this file.

rules: An entry is a name and a status. It is never evidence that a suite, method or combination is supported, secure or interoperable.
Verifiers accept only exact descriptor tuples named in their own stored request; there is no wildcard, fallback or downgrade.
A (suite, mapping, method, linking, authority, source evidence) tuple absent from combinations is unsupported.
status describes component source only. adapter_available is false for every entry in draft 0; a consumer MUST NOT register an entry as an executable vcq method from its status.

issuer-authenticated source evidence requires the verifier-pinned authorization binding of spec §4.2 rule 9 (issuer or controller, key identity, exact suite and curve or algorithm, explicit assertion authorization), checked through the suite's profile over the verified credential bytes: Data Integrity envelopes against the signed issuer, verificationMethod and assertionMethod proofPurpose; JOSE/COSE envelopes against the protected-header key identifier and algorithm and the authenticated issuer claim; direct pinned-key suites against the pinned key and any signed issuer claim the suite carries. No profile requires envelope fields its suite lacks. Key authorization comes only from verifier trust material, never from holder or presentation metadata; a signature verifying under a caller-supplied or presentation-located key is not issuer authentication. Unpinned authorization is unsupported and a wrong issuer, key, suite, curve, algorithm or purpose is policy-rejected.

conformance_vectors are illustrative proposals; none has been executed. Each applies entry resolves to an id in this registry, per enumerations.vector_applies, and says where a vector would apply, never that it passes.

Binding a field into the statement (binding) is not enforcing a predicate on a hidden witness (enforces). An obligation with no enforcer is unsupported, whatever policy digest the request or challenge hashes.
Identifiers are short forms of id_prefix plus id; they are proposals and do not occur in source. current_api values name existing items.
No entry is externally audited (sq-qhy4), and no entry makes a security, privacy or conformance claim.

entry_status.implemented-experimental: Component source exists behind an opt-in feature or detached workspace. It says nothing about a vcq adapter; see adapter_available.
entry_status.standalone-prototype: Executable experiment with a fixed relation; no library API and no RDF input.
entry_status.delegation-seam: An interface exists, but verification is delegated to a host component that sparq does not supply.
entry_status.existing-not-adapted: Existing verifier path outside this protocol's contracts.
entry_status.planned: Named in design records; not implemented.
entry_status.proposed: Introduced by this draft; not implemented.

vector_applies.method:<id>: every listed version of the query_methods entry with that id
vector_applies.method:<id>@<n>: only version n of that query method
vector_applies.suite:<id>: the authenticity_suites entry with that id, at import
vector_applies.map:<id>: the mapping_profiles entry with that id
vector_applies.link:<id>: the linking_profiles entry with that id

authenticity_suites.verified_where: inside the Noir selected-support relation and by the legacy manifest verifier
authenticity_suites.note: Schnorr over Baby-JubJub signing a Poseidon2 graph commitment, its salt and a status reference.
authenticity_suites.issuer_authorization: direct pinned-key profile (spec §4.2 rule 9): verifier trust policy pins the issuer keys authorized to assert; the signed message carries no Data Integrity or JOSE fields, and none are required

authenticity_suites.note: Reaches query methods only through trusted re-attestation; zk:sourceCryptosuite is provenance, not an in-proof property.
authenticity_suites.issuer_authorization: caller-delegated: verification uses caller-supplied key bytes and vc_bridge_json returns verification_method for the caller to bind; an import primitive, not end-to-end issuer authentication (spec §4.2 rule 9)

authenticity_suites.note: P-256/SHA-256 and P-384/SHA-384 profiles are resolved from the issuer key; P-521 is rejected. Same re-attestation limit as eddsa-rdfc-2022.

authenticity_suites.verified_where: host-supplied verifier only; the in-repo default rejects every suite

authenticity_suites.note: JSON signature modes are planned and not implemented.
Not implemented. Would bind exact payload octets; unprotected headers never enter the dataset.

authenticity_suites.representation: synthetic BLS12-381 scalar tuple [schema, subject, amount]
authenticity_suites.note: Not W3C bbs-2023 and not an RDF credential.

mapping_profiles.input: RDF triples of one credential graph
mapping_profiles.output: RDFC-1.0 canonical triples committed with string-canonical term encoding and a per-graph blank-node salt

mapping_profiles.input: RDF triples of one credential graph
mapping_profiles.output: dual-leaf commitment behind the dual-leaf feature
mapping_profiles.note: Research dial. Selected-support members accept string-canonical commitments only; resolve_circuit rejects illegal (method, circuit) pairs.

mapping_profiles.input: JSON-LD verifiable credential secured with a Data Integrity proof
mapping_profiles.output: RDF triples by expansion against a caller-supplied context allowlist, without network access
mapping_profiles.note: Named-graph expansion and proof arrays are refused. The draft additionally requires context content digests in verifier configuration and a fixed expansion base IRI.

versions.1: exact N-Triples bytes of one default graph
versions.2: exact N-Quads bytes plus an explicit IRI-named graph catalog, including empty graphs
versions.3: the version 2 source container under a version 3 domain that also binds canonicalization and DESCRIBE policy

mapping_profiles.note: SHA-256 over a versioned domain, policy, salt and exact source bytes. Not RDF canonicalization; equivalent serializations differ; reusing an anchor is publicly linkable; no issuer authentication.
Would require pinned context content digests and a fixed expansion base IRI, because a JCS signature covers context IRIs, not their content.
Would map exact authenticated payload octets only.

query_methods.query_profile: SELECT DISTINCT over a nonempty positive BGP with joins and directly bound canonical nonnegative xsd:integer comparisons up to u64::MAX; ASK, dataset clauses, GRAPH, query blank nodes, modifiers and subqueries rejected; released blank nodes and triple terms rejected
query_methods.value_domain: canonical nonnegative xsd:integer lexical forms up to u64::MAX; proposed vcq class for a hidden noncanonical form such as "018": unsupported at prepare, not unsatisfiable (current ResultError does not distinguish these)

enforces.authenticity: relation: Schnorr over commitment, salt and status reference against issuer slots in the trusted set
enforces.mapping: relation: membership of the hidden triples in the signed string-canonical commitment
enforces.status: relation: status reference against the verifier's accepted status-policy root
enforces.query: relation for the derived layout; host-public for the exact query string
enforces.audience_validity: none today; host-public over the stored request once the derived challenge binds it

query_methods.artifact_identity: The verifier derives the member from issuer-slot count, private-filter count, integer capacity and status depth, then regenerates its canonical key locally after checking nargo 1.0.0-beta.21 and bb 5.0.0-nightly.20260324 (noir-recursive). No key digest is pinned in verifier configuration.

binding.query: proved derived layout; exact query string checked on host

adapter_gaps: typed claim with enforcers, source evidence and completeness

query_methods.query_profile: as the unsigned method, with canonical signed xsd:integer comparisons in the i64 range
query_methods.value_domain: canonical signed xsd:integer lexical forms in the i64 range; proposed vcq class for a hidden noncanonical form: unsupported at prepare, not unsatisfiable

binding.query: proved derived layout; exact query string checked on host

current_api.error: sparq_proved_evaluator::Error; the model's EvaluationError for native evaluation

enforces.mapping: journaled exact-source-bytes commitment over the evaluated bytes
enforces.query: guest evaluation over the committed bytes, journaled
enforces.anchor: host-public: journaled commitment compared with the verifier anchor under verifier-agreed-anchor authority only

capacities.note: Requests may lower these; version 3 adds canonicalization ceilings.

query_methods.artifact_identity: ArtifactPin { sha256, image_id } from verifier configuration, checked by AcceptedGuest::from_artifact; only succinct receipts with development mode off are accepted.

binding.scope_anchor: journaled and compared with the verifier anchor

query_methods.request_digest_encoding: SHA-256 over a versioned domain tag, a length and serde_json bytes of the Rust request; deterministic for one build, not a wire profile
query_methods.challenge_note: A failed attempt leaves the challenge unconsumed until expiry. vcq requires an atomic consume admitting at most one success per challenge. Nonces (zk/sparql-evaluator/host/src/lib.rs:42) is a relying-party trait documented as atomic persistent acceptance; the host supplies no production store, so an adapter depends on the deployment's implementation for this property.
disclosure_inventory: journal: request digest, dataset commitment (linkable when reused), provenance and result
query_methods.caveat: Inherits the upstream RISC Zero privacy-assurance limitation and advisory GHSA-5xgj-pmjj-gw49 recorded in skills/zk-query-proofs/references/exact-evaluator.md; no privacy property is claimed.
adapter_gaps: no credential authentication or status enforcer

query_methods.note: Per-graph scan composition with FILTER, JOIN, revocation, hidden-issuer and holder proof-of-possession tiers. Its statement matches neither mode of this draft and is not mapped.

related_prototypes.relation: income - 12 * rent >= threshold over two BBS+ signed [schema, subject, amount] tuples, with unsigned 32-bit range constraints
related_prototypes.backend_selector: only dock-legogroth16-bls12-381; noir-bn254 is rejected at backend selection
related_prototypes.setup: fresh local circuit-specific setup; no production ceremony

linking_profiles.establishes: One proof relation checks signature, membership, status and query over one witness.
A released value authenticated in-relation is checked by the verifier outside the circuit.
The proof evaluates exactly the bytes whose commitment it journals. It says nothing about who endorsed the commitment (scope authority) and authenticates nothing (source evidence none).
An importer verifies a source suite and re-signs a sparq commitment; only the re-signing key is checked in-proof.
linking_profiles.evidence: components exist separately (vc_bridge ingest, Poseidon2SchnorrV1 signing); no end-to-end path checked

linking_profiles.establishes: One composite proof equates hidden signed messages and circuit inputs in one scalar field.
Equality between BLS12-381 and BN254 witnesses.
linking_profiles.evidence: none; every request needing it fails closed

combinations.note: The linking profile is the same under both authorities; a holder-declared request keeps holder-declared provenance.
The claim would name the re-attesting key, not the source issuer.
